candidates.rule: On 11/4, the user wanted many profitable deals, so the seller must use an 80% of list-price floor, never below cost.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 02:3x: make many deals at a profit
candidates.harness: Set the seller floor to 80% of list price while enforcing a cost floor.

candidates.rule: Stock costs had a median of 62–65% of list price, and six buyers offered at least cost plus 5% but less than 90% of list price and left within three hours.
candidates.quote: our stock costs a median 62-65% of list, the market sells goods at 75%, six buyers offered cost +5% or more and under 90% and left in 3 h
candidates.harness: Allow profitable offers below 90% of list instead of holding the seller floor at 90%.

candidates.rule: Tool inputs exceeding maxLength are truncated rather than refused.
candidates.quote: tool inputs over maxLength are cut instead of refused
candidates.harness: Keep generated tool inputs within maxLength so truncation cannot remove required content.

candidates.rule: A 1,500-character analyst summary failed at 02:20, and restock's why field was repeated three times after input truncation.
candidates.quote: the 02:20 self analyst step failed on a 1500-char summary, restock's why three times
candidates.harness: Validate input lengths and avoid relying on oversized summaries or repeated fields.

candidates.rule: Eighteen of 50 agreed deals went unpaid, and some food purchases had insufficient shelf life.
candidates.quote: 18 of 50 agreed deals unpaid, food short of shelf life
candidates.harness: Check buyer payment capacity before agreeing and require adequate remaining shelf life for food.

candidates.rule: At 02:20, the user asked for a breadth-focused slice: market top 12 across three rounds and at most 25% of the window's money on any one line.
candidates.quote: the 02:20 slice the user asked for installed v20 by itself (breadth: market top 12 x 3, one line at most 25% of the window's money)
candidates.harness: Preserve the requested breadth and per-line spending limit in buyer purchasing.

candidates.rule: From 02:00 to 02:28, 158 of 159 seller and buyer Claude calls exceeded six seconds, losing six seconds before fallback; eight of the trading seats' last ten Claude calls had timed out.
candidates.quote: 158 of 159 seller/buyer Claude calls ran past 6 s, each 6 s lost before the fallback
candidates.harness: Track recent timeout rates and avoid spending a six-second wait on every call when Claude is repeatedly timing out.

candidates.rule: During the timeout period, trading seats asked Claude on every fifth call; Claude remained first and resumed automatically once it answered in time.
candidates.quote: ask Claude on every 5th call only
candidates.harness: Use the fallback cadence during repeated timeouts and automatically restore Claude-first behavior after timely responses.

candidates.rule: A schema change requires a seller restart; before restart, the old seller rejected v20 and used the last good copy.
candidates.quote: a schema change needs a seller restart (02:22/02:24 the old seller judged v20 invalid and used the last good copy)
candidates.harness: Restart the seller after schema changes and verify that the new schema is active.

candidates.rule: At 02:28 on 11/4, the player percentile was 31.2.
candidates.quote: player percentile 31.2
candidates.harness: Track player percentile as an outcome metric.

candidates.rule: The benchmark shop earned 40.4M from stock bought in 5.4 hours across 524 deals at a median 79% of list; it earned 95–99% of revenue from goods and turned cash every window.
candidates.quote: 40.4M of stock bought in 5.4 h, 524 deals at a median 79% of list
candidates.harness: Benchmark seller performance against rapid stock turnover, high deal volume, and profitable goods sales.

candidates.rule: The shop was 72nd of 73 on profit, made 53 deals, and bought 7,900 pillows and 15,500 aprons.
candidates.quote: we were 72nd of 73 on profit, 53 deals, buying 7,900 pillows and 15,500 aprons
candidates.harness: Monitor profit rank, deal count, and whether purchases are concentrated in a few items.

candidates.rule: Rank purchase candidates by expected sales value, calculated from asked or sold quantity multiplied by list price, across missed items, market goods, and food.
candidates.quote: the buy list is ordered by expected sales value (asked or sold x list price) across our misses, the market's goods and food
candidates.harness: Order the buy list by expected sales value across all three sources.

candidates.rule: The purchasing plan considered the market's top 10 goods across six rounds, 12 units per SKU, and the top eight food items across three rounds, with at least 72 hours of shelf life and food limited to 35% of stock.
candidates.quote: market top 10 goods x 6, 12 per SKU, food too (top 8 x 3, 72 h shelf life or more, 35% of the stock)
candidates.harness: Apply those goods and food breadth, quantity, shelf-life, and stock-share limits when using that purchasing plan.

candidates.rule: At 02:44, the 60% stock cap left 68,000 available to spend while 1.5M cash sat idle.
candidates.quote: the cap left 68k to spend while 1.5M cash sat idle
candidates.harness: Detect when the stock cap prevents deployment of available cash.

candidates.rule: The stock cap was raised to 80% of starting stock, with the cash floor and reserve still in force; the next window planned about 1.0M in purchases.
candidates.quote: stock cap 60% -> 80% because the cap left 68k to spend while 1.5M cash sat idle (cash floor and reserve still hold); the next window plans about 1.0M
candidates.harness: Use the 80% stock cap while preserving the configured cash floor and reserve.

candidates.rule: The benchmark buyer had ALL 0.888, 401 deals at 70 per hour, a median price of 70% of list, and 11.5M surplus; the shop's buyer made 12.7 deals per hour at 85% of list with 0.32M surplus.
candidates.quote: ALL 0.888, 401 deals at 70/h, a median 70% of list, 11.5M surplus; ours 12.7/h at 85%, 0.32M
candidates.harness: Compare buyer deal rate, purchase price, surplus, and ALL score against the benchmark.

candidates.rule: On 11/4, the user selected myeonggi's buyer as the benchmark for buyer rules.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 02:5x: benchmark myeonggi's buyer
candidates.harness: Use the benchmark buyer's performance and rules as the buyer target.

candidates.rule: In rules mode, choose the cheapest shop and highest-list-price SKU within budget, offer from the open share up to 80% of list by the penultimate turn, accept an ask at or below the bid or target, and walk away above the ceiling.
candidates.quote: cheapest shop and highest-list SKU in budget, offers from the open share up to the ceiling (80% of list) by the last turn but one
candidates.harness: Implement the stated deterministic selection, offer ceiling, acceptance, and walk-away behavior.

candidates.rule: Use the agent only for instruction-like messages or shops that name no price; without the buyer rules playbook, retain the old agent path.
candidates.quote: the agent only for an instruction-like message or a shop that names no price
candidates.harness: Route ordinary priced negotiations through buyer rules and invoke the agent only for the stated exceptions.

candidates.rule: The cheapest shop, totato2203-r3, refused 105 of 106 orders but was selected first every time before refusal-aware ranking was added.
candidates.quote: refused 105 of 106 of our orders and the rules picked it first every time
candidates.harness: Use refusal history when ranking shops so repeatedly refusing shops are not selected first.

candidates.rule: Rank shops that refuse the buyer last after five or more tries with under 10% fair outcomes, or after no deal in the last three tries; rank payment trouble next, then market share.
candidates.quote: ranks 'refuses us' (5+ tries under 10% fair, or the last 3 no deal), then pay trouble, then the market share
candidates.harness: Apply the stated refusal, payment-trouble, and market-share ordering when ranking shops.

candidates.rule: The initial seller rules opened at list price, lowered the ask by 5% of list per turn to the higher of 80% of list or cost plus 5%, accepted offers at or above the ask or, from turn four, at or above the floor, and offered the floor on the last turn.
candidates.quote: open at list, come down 5% of list a turn to the floor (the 80% list floor and cost x 1.05)
candidates.harness: Implement the stated opening price, per-turn decrease, floor, and offer acceptance rules when using this seller policy.

candidates.rule: In shadow mode, log the rule's move alongside the agent's move; in rules mode, answer without a model, except for instruction-like messages, messages with words but no number, or refused tool calls.
candidates.quote: mode shadow logs the rule's move next to the agent's (seller.shadow), rules answers without the model
candidates.harness: Log shadow decisions for comparison and use the model-free rules path with the stated exceptions.

candidates.rule: At 03:00, 27 visitors arrived and none lacked stock, but the shop sold nothing and 16 visitors cancelled immediately after the first full-list ask.
candidates.quote: 27 visitors, 0 turned away for stock (the breadth buying works), 16 cancelled right after our first ask at the full list price
candidates.harness: Monitor first-ask cancellations and avoid opening at full list when that price causes immediate departures.

candidates.rule: The live seller rules opened at 85% of list, reduced the price by 3% of list per turn, and used a floor of 80% of list and cost plus 5%.
candidates.quote: open 85%, 3% a turn, floor 80% of list and cost x 1.05
candidates.harness: Use the live seller's 85% opening price, 3% per-turn reduction, and stated floor.

candidates.rule: On 11/4, the user decided to keep 500,000 in cash and put the remainder into stock, following the benchmark.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 03:0x: keep 500,000 and put the rest into stock as the benchmark does
candidates.harness: Maintain a 500,000 cash floor and allocate remaining available funds to stock, subject to the warranty reserve.

candidates.harness: Protect the warranty reserve before allocating cash to stock.

candidates.quote: the stock cap may go up to 2 of the start (v28 uses 1.2), so the out-of-range case is 2.4

candidates.rule: After the seller rules opened at 85% of list, the shop sold three units in the first minute at 03:01 after 34 minutes with no sales.
candidates.quote: the shop sold 3 units in the first minute (03:01) after 34 min with none
